assessment: We believe that this study will make significant contributions to developmental neuroscience and vision science as it is a novel attempt to study the processes that might be innate or genetically wired and those that emerge due to worldly experiences within the sensory systems. The authors suggest that early postnatal experience and time spent inside the womb differentially shape the structural and functional development of the visual cortex. The use of large neonatal dataset from the developmental Human Connectome Project is impressive and strengthens the claims made in the paper.
